rounds.text: Milestone Global Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 8.35x and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.87x against a book value of ₹ 21.2 [E1, E2]. These valuation multiples sit at a steep discount to sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E is 24.85x and EV/EBITDA is 12.55x compared to the company's 4.81x [E6, E11]. Fundamental momentum is sharply accelerating, demonstrated by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 31% and profit growth of 247% [E17, E21], alongside a quarterly operating margin reaching 12% in September 2026 [E31]. The balance sheet offers robust downside protection, featuring a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 5.33x [E37, E38]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive intrinsic valuation gap with a margin of safety of 79.4%, while the current market price implies an overly pessimistic -3.7% earnings growth [E44, E45, E46]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 1.17% over the past five years and recorded negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.29 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E54].

Conceded: [E44]. Despite low valuation multiples on paper, Milestone Global Ltd suffers from a severe cash flow disconnect, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.29 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -0.39 Cr in March 2026 alongside a poor cash conversion ratio of -0.39x [E34, E35, E36]. Top-line expansion has historically stalled, demonstrated by a dismal compounded sales growth of 1% over five years and -3% over three years, while operating margins remain strictly inconsistent [E15, E16, E32]. Return profiles are persistently lacklustre, marked by a median return on equity of just 5% over 10 years and 7% over 5 years, accompanied by a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4, E26, E27, E53]. Furthermore, domestic institutional investors have been quietly reducing their stake, trimming holdings from 5.98% in December 2023 to 5.32% in September 2026, while the stock languishes at a mere 17% of its 52-week range [E5, E42].

Conceded: [E34, E35, E36]. However, the focus on historical top-line stagnation [E15, E16] ignores an explosive current inflection, led by a 31% trailing twelve month sales growth and a 247% trailing twelve month profit growth [E17, E21]. Results are accelerating dramatically—evidenced by a recent quarterly net profit surge of 820% YoY and an operating margin jumping to 12% in September 2026—meaning stale multi-year averages completely miss the active turnaround [E31, E59, E62]. The bear's critique of historical ROE [E26, E27] overlooks that the company's current ROE of 10.48% and ROCE of 11.95% handily outperform sector benchmarks of 6.04% and 6.13% respectively [E9, E10]. Conceded: [E4]. Despite zero dividends [E4], the business is virtually debt-free with a pristine 0.01x debt-to-equity ratio and robust short-term liquidity of 5.33x, while strong promoter confidence is visible in their steady 73.26% stake [E37, E38, E41]. Finally, the minor institutional trimming cited [E42] is dwarfed by a massive margin of safety where today's depressed price of 18.5 implies a negative 3.7% earnings growth, completely disconnecting current market pessimism from actual operational velocity [E44, E46].

Conceded: [E31, E59]. While the bull points to an explosive TTM sales growth of 31% [E17] and profit growth of 247% [E21], it ignores the deeper multi-year structural malaise where 3-year compounded sales growth sits at -3% [E16] and 5-year sales growth is a meager 1% [E15]. Conceded: [E9, E10]. Despite those current profitability metrics outpacing sector benchmarks, the company's historical performance tells a different story with a 10-year median ROE of just 5% [E26] and a 3-year median ROE of 6% [E28], demonstrating that current elevated returns may simply reflect cyclical noise rather than sustainable competitive advantage. Conceded: [E37, E41]. The pristine debt-to-equity and steady promoter stake do not negate the alarming cash conversion of -0.39x and negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.29 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E35], meaning soaring reported profits are failing to materialize as actual cash. Finally, the bull's reliance on a wide margin of safety [E45] glosses over the fact that domestic institutions have quietly reduced their holdings to 5.32% [E42] and the stock sits languishing at a mere 17% of its 52-week range [E5].
